newsitem.title: SPAIN: Venezuela reaches deal with Iberia on Viasa.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela reaches deal with Iberia on Viasa.

text.p: Venzuela reached an agreement on Tuesday with Iberia to save Venezuela's struggling national airline Viasa from bankruptcy, Spain's state holding group SEPI said.
SEPI said the President of Venezuela's National Investment Fund (FIV) Alberto Poletto had agreed with Iberia's chairman Xabier de Irala to channel further funds into the loss-making airline.
"The measures proposed are essential to avoid VIASA's bankrutpcy and guarantee its survival," SEPI, state-owned Iberia's major shareholder, said in a statement.
State-owned Spanish carrier Iberia holds a 45 percent stake in Viasa, while Venezuela has a 40 percent share.
Under the agreement, Iberia has agreed to recapitalise part of Viasa's debt in exchange for the fleet of aircraft that was being held as guarantee.

"Iberia and FIV believe, however, that a basic requisite for the plan to work is the modification of Viasa's labour conditions, including a revision of all the collective agreements," SEPI said. The two sides said they would agree the details on the exact amount of the debt and value of assets in the next few days.
But they acknowledged the plan hinged on agreement from Viasa's workers, a factor which stalled a previous emergency plan.

Iberia spearheaded a plan last November to save the loss-making Venezuelan airline from bankruptcy. But the plan, which involved cutting jobs, freezing pay and discarding unprofitable routes was overwhelmingly rejected by Viasa's workers, who claimed it failed to guarantee the future of the company. Iberia then withdrew its offer.
The two sides said they also decided to look for another party to run the airline. In the meantime, the two will split the management and administrative responsibilities.
SEPI said Iberia and FIV would maintain the suspension of flights until the plan had been approved and a definite solution for the company had been reached.
The airline suspended all its flights on Thursday for at least two weeks, stranding hundreds of passengers.
